title: Rigveda 10.179: To Indra
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.179: To Indra: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.179 is a hymn of 3 verses addressed to Indra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 151r-151v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.179.1 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 37); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 151r
translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>ut ti̍ṣṭha̱tāva̍ paśya̱tendra̍sya bhā̱gam ṛ̱tviya̍m | yadi̍ śrā̱to ju̱hota̍na̱ yady aśrā̍to mama̱ttana̍ ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>Now lift ye up yourselves and look on Indra's seasonable share. If it be ready, offer it; unready, ye have been remise.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 151r (OPenn image 150, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.178.1 ‹sahāvānaṁ tarutāraṁ rathānām›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 151v, begins in RV 10.179.2 ‹vimadhyam›. Verse 10.179.1 ends on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.179.2-3 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 37); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 151v
translation.original_text:
2śrā̱taṁ ha̱vir o ṣv i̍ndra̱ pra yā̍hi ja̱gāma̱ sūro̱ adhva̍no̱ vima̍dhyam | pari̍ tvāsate ni̱dhibhi̱ḥ sakhā̍yaḥ kula̱pā na vrā̱japa̍ti̱ṁ cara̍ntam ||
3śrā̱tam ma̍nya̱ ūdha̍ni śrā̱tam a̱gnau suśrā̍tam manye̱ tad ṛ̱taṁ navī̍yaḥ | mādhya̍ṁdinasya̱ sava̍nasya da̱dhnaḥ pibe̍ndra vajrin purukṛj juṣā̱ṇaḥ ||
translation.text:
2Oblation is prepared: come to us, Indra; the Sun hath travelled over half his journey. Friends with their stores are sitting round thee waiting like lords of clans for the tribe's wandering chieftain.
3Dressed in the udder and on fire, I fancy; well-dressed, I fancy, is this recent present. Drink, Indra, of the curd of noon's libation with favour, Thunderer, thou whose deeds are mighty.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 151v (OPenn image 151, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.179.2 ‹vimadhyam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 152r, begins in RV 10.180.3 ‹vāmam ojo 'jāyathā vṛṣabha›. Verses 10.179.2-3 end on this page; 10.179.2 begins on fol. 151r.
